name: Ring Dermoid of Cornea

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Ophthalmologic Diagnostic Criteria for Corneal Dermoids

criteria.description: Presence of a circumferential, elevated, opaque, and keratinized lesion involving the peripheral cornea
Histological confirmation showing choristomatous tissue with epidermal and dermal elements including hair follicles and sebaceous glands
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) or ultrasound biomicroscopy demonstrating lesion depth and corneal involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesion plus histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and confirmed by histopathology when excision is performed.

pathognomonic.notes: Distinctive ring-shaped lesion at the corneal periphery

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of hair follicles on corneal surface
pathognomonic.notes: Ectopic hair growth on corneal dermoid

common.symptomName: Visual axis obstruction causing decreased visual acuity
common.notes: Depending on lesion size and location
searchTerms: blocked vision due to corneal opacity
blurred sight from visual axis blockage

common.notes: Light sensitivity due to corneal irritation

occasional.notes: Irregular corneal curvature induced by lesion
Reflex tearing due to corneal surface abnormality
Secondary to lesion involvement of limbal area

rare.notes: Due to chronic irritation or trauma

rare.symptomName: Corneal scarring leading to permanent vision loss
searchTerms: permanent vision impairment from corneal damage
scar tissue on cornea affecting sight

rare.notes: Rare complication secondary to lesion irritation

imaging: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing lesion depth and corneal involvement
other: Histopathology revealing choristomatous tissue with epidermal and dermal elements including hair follicles and sebaceous glands

distinguishingFeatures: Typically localized to limbus rather than forming a complete ring
Smaller size and less circumferential involvement
Progressive fibrovascular growth from conjunctiva onto cornea
Lacks hair follicles and keratinized surface

redFlags: Development of corneal ulceration or infection
Significant visual axis obstruction causing amblyopia in children
references: Krachmer JH, Mannis MJ, Holland EJ. Cornea. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2011.
